entries.title: Ask HN: Are you working on interesting technical problems?
entries.author: obsession
entries.current_title: Ask HN: Are you working on interesting technical problems?
entries.excerpt: I have been feeling disappointed that I haven't been able to use my computer science degree to it's full potential. Most of my work seems to be boring CRUD work where the challenge is gluing libraries together or figuring out business requirements. Actual interesting technical problems seems to be mostly wrapped in ready-made libraries / SaaS services. Anyone in the same boat?

entries.title: Ask HN: What is the first thing you implement at a new company?
entries.author: systemtest
entries.current_title: Ask HN: What is the first thing you implement at a new company?
entries.excerpt: For job-hoppers and contractors. If you arrive at a company, what is the first thing you push for? For instance, I usually implement a good feature-branch flow with branch pipelines and a strict merge-to-develop etiquette with mandatory merge requests. It makes my work easier and once the team is used to it, they also really like it. No more messy development branches. I also request a small office stool next to my desk to make code reviews, three amigos and pair programming
entries.guide_zh: 换到一家新公司后，你最先推动落实什么工具、流程或实践？
